subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance be bounded by default, and should the permanent cancellation/fencing contract use this new config key plus the shared command-queue onTaskTimeout callback?
rationale: Source review can validate the mitigation, but cannot choose the product default, permanent operator configuration burden, or shared queue API ownership without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt a bounded default
options.body: Use a finite host-owned default or existing safety budget, retain the proven fence, and provide an explicit opt-out for engines that legitimately require longer maintenance.

options.title: Keep the opt-in mitigation
options.body: Merge the disabled-by-default configuration and accept that affected operators must discover and enable the workaround.

options.title: Define cancellation first
options.body: Pause this branch and establish a cooperative context-engine cancellation or existing-signal contract before adding permanent configuration and callback surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt a bounded default
recommendation.body: Use a finite host-owned default or existing safety budget, retain the proven fence, and provide an explicit opt-out for engines that legitimately require longer maintenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans both the shared queue timeout machinery and stalled-session recovery policy, making them the strongest available owner for this cross-cutting decision.
